about: A command-line tool that turns the output of common Linux commands into JSON.

prs.title: Failed systemd services are listed correctly
prs.broken: On newer systemd, the list of failed services also included junk rows taken from the help footer, so 2 failed services showed as 6.
prs.changed: I made the reader stop at the new footer as well as the old one.
prs.matters: Scripts that check for failed services see the real count.

prs.title: Swap sizes with decimals no longer crash
prs.broken: Reading plain swapon output crashed when a size had a decimal point, like 2.2G, which is how it usually prints.
prs.changed: I made sizes read as decimal numbers and then turned into whole bytes.
prs.matters: Swap usage can be read on ordinary machines without an error.

prs.title: Reading ss output for TCP or UDP no longer crashes
prs.broken: Turning the output of ss -t or ss -u into JSON crashed, because those commands leave out one column the reader expected.
prs.changed: I made rows without that column read the same way, just without that field.
prs.matters: Common network checks like listing listening ports now work.
